triage.name: Acute appendicitis
triage.reason: Classic undifferentiated abdominal pain case with a clear diagnosis reachable by history, exam, labs and imaging, and important look-alikes.

family_history: Appendicitis in a parent or sibling

chief_complaints.text: Pain started around my belly button and moved to the lower right

hpi.duration: Usually less than 48 hours at presentation
hpi.progression: Starts as vague periumbilical pain, then localizes to the right lower quadrant within 12–24 hours and becomes constant
hpi.location: Periumbilical at first, then right lower quadrant
hpi.quality: Dull and crampy at first, then sharp and constant

associated_symptoms.text: Vomiting that began after the pain

pertinent_negatives: Sick contacts with the same illness

argues_against: Colicky flank pain radiating to the groin
Sudden one-sided pelvic pain with vomiting

atypical.how_it_differs: Young children can't describe pain migration; they present with irritability, vomiting and refusal to walk.
Milder pain, little fever and a lower white count despite more advanced disease.
Later in pregnancy the appendix is displaced upward, so pain can be in the right flank or upper quadrant.

general.mild: Uncomfortable but not toxic; lies still
general.moderate: Lies still, avoids moving, winces with the car ride or cough

findings.maneuver: Palpate all four quadrants, starting away from the pain
Press at McBurney point (one-third from the ASIS to the umbilicus)
Press in the left lower quadrant
findings.finding: Pain felt in the right lower quadrant

findings.maneuver: Extend the right hip with the patient on the left side
Internally rotate the flexed right hip
Ask the patient to cough, or tap the heel (gentler than releasing deep pressure)
findings.finding: Pain with jarring, suggesting peritoneal irritation

findings.maneuver: Pelvic exam when a gynecologic cause is possible
findings.finding: No cervical motion tenderness or adnexal mass

labs.caveat: A normal white count doesn't rule out appendicitis, especially early or in older adults.
Rises more after 24 hours; higher values suggest perforation.
Mild sterile pyuria from an inflamed appendix next to the ureter or bladder; can mislead toward a urinary infection.
Negative. Required in anyone who could be pregnant before imaging; rules out ectopic pregnancy.

imaging.study: Ultrasound of the right lower quadrant
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast

findings.text: Dilated appendix over 6 mm with wall thickening and enhancement

imaging.study: MRI abdomen and pelvis without contrast

findings.text: Usually nonspecific; occasionally a calcified appendicolith

initial.why: Leukocytosis with left shift supports inflammation
Looks for urinary infection or a stone
Rules out pregnancy and ectopic pregnancy before imaging

confirmatory.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
confirmatory.why: Most accurate test in nonpregnant adults

confirmatory.test: Ultrasound of the right lower quadrant
confirmatory.why: First choice in children and pregnancy

supporting.why: Adds to the white count in scoring and suggests perforation when high

not_indicated.why: No role in right lower quadrant pain
Not needed unless the pain is epigastric

decision_points: Pregnancy test before CT in anyone who could be pregnant
Ultrasound first in children and pregnancy; CT if nondiagnostic in nonpregnant patients
Peritonitis or instability goes to surgery without waiting for imaging

differential.name: Ectopic pregnancy
differential.why_considered: Lower abdominal pain in someone who could be pregnant
differential.trigger: Any patient who could be pregnant

imaging: No intrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal ultrasound

differential.name: Ovarian torsion
differential.why_considered: Sudden one-sided lower abdominal pain with vomiting
differential.trigger: Abrupt onset with vomiting at the start

imaging: Enlarged ovary with reduced Doppler flow

differential.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
differential.why_considered: Lower abdominal pain and fever in a sexually active patient

history: Colicky flank pain radiating to the groin

differential.name: Mesenteric adenitis
differential.why_considered: Right lower quadrant pain in a child after a viral illness

imaging: Enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes with a normal appendix

differential.name: Crohn disease
differential.why_considered: Right lower quadrant pain from terminal ileitis

severity.mild: Early, uncomplicated: less than 24 hours, localized tenderness, low-grade or no fever
severity.moderate: Established, uncomplicated: guarding, fever, clear leukocytosis
severity.severe: Perforated with a localized abscess or phlegmon
severity.critical: Free perforation with diffuse peritonitis and sepsis

red_flags.meaning: Generalized peritonitis; needs a surgeon now

red_flags.finding: Sudden relief of pain followed by worse, spreading pain

complications.name: Adhesive small bowel obstruction
clues: Prior appendectomy with new distension and vomiting

special_populations.differences: Younger children perforate more often because diagnosis is delayed; ultrasound first.
Atypical, milder findings and higher perforation rates.
Most common non-obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy; pain may be higher; ultrasound then MRI.

key_questions.question: Where did the pain start, and has it moved?
key_questions.looking_for: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant

key_questions.question: When did it start?
key_questions.looking_for: Hours to under 2 days; longer suggests perforation

key_questions.question: Did the vomiting start before or after the pain?
Could you be pregnant? When was your last period?
Any vaginal discharge or bleeding?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; present suggests PID or ectopic pregnancy

key_questions.question: Any burning with urination or blood in the urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent; present suggests a urinary cause

key_questions.question: Have you had your appendix out or other abdominal surgery?

reasoning_points: Pain migrating from the periumbilical area to the right lower quadrant
Anorexia and vomiting after the pain began
Localized right lower quadrant tenderness with peritoneal signs

medium: Retrocecal appendix: flank pain, positive psoas sign, little anterior tenderness
Woman of reproductive age with gynecologic look-alikes
hard: Older adult with mild pain and a normal white count
Pregnant patient with right upper quadrant pain
Toddler with vomiting and refusal to walk
Presents after perforation with diffuse pain

review.notes: Reference example for prompts; needs clinician review like any other profile.
